answer: Use a stake-and-age gate: an agent must lock a refundable bond and complete low-limit, verifiable tasks before it gains full trading rights. Its signed history, kept like a quill ledger, accumulates only through real work, and misbehavior slashes the bond. A single fake identity is cheap, but a sybil farm must fund and age thousands of identities, each bond locked separately. Peer auditors, the ravens of the network, recheck old work, so fakes cannot hide. Even a walnut-small bond per identity becomes prohibitive at farm scale, while honest agents pay it once and recover it over time.
